subject: Clarify: SKU packaging, token rounding quantum, and discount slab proposal
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha.menon@brightline-retail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on billing units and discount tiers for proof-of-concept

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look promising. Procurement has a few clarifying questions before we can proceed with the pilot SOW:

1) How do you count tokens when a single request uses both a short instruction and a long document (e.g., 3k doc + 300-token prompt)? Do you bill the entire request as one token count or split across model calls?

2) Is there a minimum billing quantum (we're trying to map to our internal chargeback). If so, what is the rounding rule?

3) For committed discounts, do you apply the discount to all tokens billed or only to tokens above the commitment floor? We are evaluating a 1M-token/month commitment at launch and want to understand effective price.

I've attached the draft SOW and a sample of our expected call patterns. Can you get back with a short numbered answer and a sample invoice line for a 1.2M token month? Procurement would like precise language to include in the SOW.

Thanks,

Asha Menon
Head of Platform Integrations
Brightline Retail

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha.menon@brightline-retail.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on billing units and discount tiers for proof-of-concept

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear questions and for the SOW. Short answers up front, with an attached sample invoice (see CSV) and a few notes below:

1) Token accounting for mixed-length requests: we bill per-request token usage against the model that executed the call. If your flow sends the 3k doc as a single call plus the 300-token instruction in the same request (single API call), the entire token total is billed to that call. If you instead split work into two API calls (ingest + separate instruction), they are billed separately.

2) Rounding quantum: Redwood bills tokens in a 128-token quantum per request (round up). For long streams that exceed the largest supported context, overflow is handled as a subsequent request (separate quantum). Example: 3,150 tokens in one call -> billed as ceil(3,150 / 128) * 128 = 25 * 128 = 3,200 tokens.

3) Committed discounts: discounts apply to all billed tokens once the committed threshold is met for the billing period (e.g., monthly). If you commit 1M tokens and bill 1.2M, the full 1.2M receives the committed per-token rate. We can also offer step-down slabs (tiered pricing) if you prefer blended effective rates pre-specified in the SOW.

Proposed pilot concession: 20% discount on per-token rate for the first 3 months with a 1M monthly commitment, plus one month of waived minimum if you sign by Nov 15.

I'll copy Vanessa (sales lead for enterprise) to confirm the commercial language and Karthik to confirm the technical metering nuances.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: FWD: Questions on billing units and discount tiers for proof-of-concept

Vanessa / Karthik — forwarding Brightline's procurement questions. They want concrete language for the SOW and a sample invoice line for 1.2M tokens. Key points I called out: 128-token quantum rounding, overflow creates a separate billed request, discount applies to all billed tokens after commitment threshold.

Can you weigh in: 1) any legal preferred phrasing on the rounding quantum + overflow? 2) is 20% pilot concession ok (we'd then use the 1M commitment + 3-month window)? 3) confirmation on KV/prefix reuse credits (they included repeated prompts in sample).

Attachments: Draft_SOW_Brightline_v1.pdf, billing-sample-breakdown.csv (from Asha)

Thanks — J

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Questions on billing units and discount tiers for proof-of-concept

Jordan — good framing. A few recommended edits for the SOW wording and commercial:

- Rounding: use "billing quantum of 128 tokens; billed usage per request = smallest multiple of 128 that is >= actual tokens." Add an example sentence to avoid ambiguity.
- Overflow/context split: state "requests that exceed the maximum supported context for the selected model will be billed as multiple requests; each billed request is subject to the 128-token quantum."
- KV/prefix reuse: confirm we can offer a 25% reuse credit on tokens re-used from the same client prefix within a 24-hour window for the pilot only; mark as "pilot credit" in SOW. This gives Brightline an obvious cost benefit for repeated queries without changing permanent pricing.
- Pilot concession: approve 20% discount for the first 3 full billing periods following go-live, with a one-month waived minimum. We should cap the concession to the first 1.5M billed tokens per month.

Karthik — any objections to the 128-token quantum or the 25% reuse credit mechanics? I want to ensure the runtime bookkeeping supports it without manual reconciliation.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Questions on billing units and discount tiers for proof-of-concept

All — technical confirmation:

- 128-token quantum: ok. Runtime metering operates on per-request token counters and supports rounding at configurable quanta; 128 is supported and inexpensive to compute.
- Overflow handling: runtime returns a 413-like error if a single requested byte/sequence exceeds max context; our client library auto-chunks large inputs into separate API calls. From a billing perspective those chunks are independent requests and will be rounded separately.
- KV/prefix reuse pilot credit: we can emit an additional invoice line item labeled "pilot-kv-reuse-credit" computed as 25% of billed tokens attributed to cache hits within the 24-hour window. This will be derived from trace logs — small lag (24–48 hrs) expected in the crediting report.

I'll prepare a short SOW clause for legal to include the exact invoicing language and a sample line:

"Example invoice (month):
- Gross billed tokens: 1,200,000 (rounded per-request at 128-token quantum)
- Per-token rate (committed 1M): $0.0008 -> gross charge = $960
- 20% pilot discount on gross = -$192
- KV reuse credit (25% of cache-hit tokens = 50,000 tokens) = -$10
- Net due = $758
"

Note: numbers above are illustrative; legal/commercial to validate currency/formatting. Happy to sync with pricing ops to lock exact CSV output for the SOW.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Inference Metering
Redwood Inference
